text.p: Alberto Puig led a charge of home riders by setting the fastest time in Friday's opening 500cc qualifying for the Spanish Grand Prix on Sunday.

Only a last-gasp effort by world champion Michael Doohan -- who snatched second -- spoilt the day for Spanish fans, who had seen local favourite Alex Criville recover from an early fall to join Puig and Carlos Checa on the provisional front row.
Puig, still recovering from a serious accident two years ago, showed impressive form to end the session nearly half a second quicker than his rivals.
"The important thing is what happens on Sunday. I have to be realistic," said Puig, who tested his Honda extensively on the Jerez circuit earlier this season.
Fellow Honda rider Doohan delayed his challenge until the last possible moment and nudged the Honda of Checa into third plance, with Criville fourth on a similar machine.

Criville, currently second behind Doohan in the world championship, had looked shaken after clipping a kerb and crashing. But he returned to the track to keep up the pressure on his Australian team mate.
